words.lemma: táin (gen. sg., verbal noun of do-aig 'drives off', < *to-ag-ni-) + bó (gen. pl.)
táin (nom. sg.) + bó (gen. pl.), title Táin Bó Regamon
bó (nom. pl. baí) + agaid 'drives' (pres. ind. pass. 3 pl.); in the context line after the passage
βοῦς + ἀπελαύνω + ἄγω; in the context line after the passage

cognate: OIr. bó / baí ~ Gk βοῦς ~ Ved. gáv- (*gʷṓws); OIr. ag- (agaid, táin < *to-ag-ni-) ~ Gk ἄγω ~ Ved. aj- (*h₂eǵ-)
drift_or_renewal: Greek often renews the verb with ἐλαύνω / ἀπελαύνω (Il. 1.154, Arrian's ἀπελάσαι beside ἀγαγεῖν); Irish has táin as a nominalised preverb compound (do-aig, *to-ag-), the generic term for a cattle raid and a saga genre
shared_syntax: verb *h₂eǵ- with *gʷōu- as direct object (Irish passive with baí as subject; Irish nominal táin + objective genitive bó); Greek βοῦς acc. + ἄγειν
context: Cattle raiding by heroes or gods. Irish: the Táin Bó Regamon is called a forerunner of the Táin Bó Cúailnge; in the TBC the alarm call 'men are slain, women carried off, cattle driven'. Greek: Heracles is sent by Eurystheus to bring Geryon's cattle from Erytheia (Isocrates; Arrian has the same exploit). Vedic (support): Indra drives the cows out of Vala (gā́ḥ ud-ājat), and in RV 1.33.3 he 'drives together the cows of the stranger (aryáḥ gā́ḥ ajati)', i.e. rustling. The match is in the heroic-raid context, not just pastoral herding. Caveat: 'Drive cattle' is the obvious herding collocation in any language that keeps both roots, so collocation alone is weak evidence. The claim rests on the shared heroic or mythic raid setting (Táin; Heracles-Geryon; Indra-Vala), which I recall the literature treating as an inherited cattle-raid theme (Lincoln; Watkins). The Greek anchors are late prose retelling the Geryon myth, and the Irish TBC line is in a context line, not the passage line.
phrase: *gʷṓws *h₂eǵ- 'drive (off) cattle' as the term for a cattle raid

note: All 166 bundles read. Most partners share only common roots (kin terms, bʰer-, h₂neḱ-) in unrelated contexts. One medium claim: drive cattle (*h₂eǵ- + *gʷōu-), cross-bundle. Rejected: Ir. men/cattle/mother/father roscad vs AV 1.31 svasti list (generic, obscure, opposite polarity); Ir. ailid + cú vs ON ala + hundr ('rear a dog', generic); Ir. bráthair a athar/máthar vs Skt pitṛ bhrātā (descriptive kin terms); scíath ~ щитъ (BC-6645f, different collocation); 'mairc ... liatha' vs OE fealwe mēaras (Irish mairc = mairg 'woe', not 'horse'); TBC 'forbíad a ainm h-Érind co bráth' (fame motif, no cross-branch partner in the slab).
